course.title: Private PDFs: financial meaning, rendering, download and email delivery
course.description: Follow Craves documents from an authorized source snapshot through durable rendering, private storage, authenticated download and explicitly requested email. Learn how to extend the module without inventing tax invoices or resending uncertain email deliveries.

lessons.title: Identify exactly what a document proves before generating it
lessons.overview: A PDF is a presentation of facts, not authority to create new financial facts. Craves has six implemented document types: ORDER_SUMMARY, PAYMENT_RECEIPT, SUBSCRIPTION_RECEIPT, CHEF_ORDER_STATEMENT, CHEF_EARNINGS_STATEMENT and CHEF_SETTLEMENT_STATEMENT. The owning services supply saved order, subscription or finance data; Notification renders and stores it. An order summary is not payment proof. A kitchen-specific payment receipt is not the total of an entire multi-kitchen checkout. A settlement allocation is not independent evidence that a bank credited a chef. The capabilities response explicitly reports taxInvoicesEnabled=false. This training does not change that meaning or invent statutory issuer details.

steps.label: Map each type to its owner
steps.detail: Read the document catalogue in the module README and the Type enum in DocumentModels. Order owns order summaries, eligible payment receipts and chef order activity. Subscription owns paid subscription-invoice facts. Integration owns recorded chef earnings and settlement allocations. Notification must not query another service's private database directly to bypass the owned source contract.

steps.label: Understand customer receipt eligibility
steps.detail: The reviewed payment-receipt source describes a chef-specific ON_DEMAND order whose owned checkout is PAID. The subscription receipt uses an owned paid invoice and its recorded paid_at, cycle and amount, not today's plan price. Before extending eligibility, read the actual source controller and tests; do not label every created or authorized provider payment as captured.

steps.label: Keep chef totals correctly scoped
steps.detail: Chef order statements use immutable order-time ownership. Earnings totals remain separated by recorded status. Settlement statements contain only the requesting chef's allocations, never the entire shared batch total. A new statement query must prove cross-chef isolation with a shared-batch fixture, not only a single-chef happy path.

steps.label: Define period semantics
steps.detail: The From date is included and To date is excluded. The implemented browser contract accepts one to thirty-one calendar days. Document the timezone conversion and test month boundaries. Sources reject an oversized result rather than silently truncating beyond one thousand detail rows. A smaller date range is the appropriate user action, not a hidden partial financial statement.

steps.label: Preserve recorded amounts
steps.detail: The source snapshots serialize existing amounts without repricing. Do not introduce floating-point rounding, recalculate tax from today's settings or reinterpret an original total as an outstanding balance after a refund. Any new allocation or correction rule requires approved financial semantics before implementation.

steps.label: Mark statutory gaps explicitly
steps.detail: GST tax invoices, bills of supply and credit notes are not claimed by the current module. Adding them requires approved issuer identity, registration details, numbering, tax treatment and correction behavior. Keep those decisions separate from the technical ability to draw a logo and table on a page.

lessons.example: A checkout contains two kitchen orders. A payment receipt requested for one kitchen must display that kitchen order's recorded scope, not duplicate the parent checkout total. A test should include both children so an incorrectly broad query is detected.
lessons.lab: Build a six-row document meaning matrix: type, owner, eligible state, subject, period semantics, amounts and explicit non-claims. Locate the three owned source adapters named in the module README and their database tests. Design fixtures for a two-kitchen checkout, an unpaid invoice, a shared settlement batch and a thirty-two-day request. Predict each accepted or rejected result before running isolated tests. Do not create a real payment or modify finance records to make a receipt eligible.
lessons.pitfall: Professional layout does not make a document a legally valid tax invoice or bank-credit confirmation. Its financial meaning must come from approved facts and contracts.

questions.prompt: What does the current capabilities contract say about tax invoices?
options: Every PDF is automatically a tax invoice
A course completion enables tax invoices
questions.explanation: The implemented module does not claim statutory tax-invoice support.

questions.prompt: What belongs in a requesting chef's settlement statement?
questions.explanation: The source contract must enforce owner isolation even inside a shared settlement batch.

questions.prompt: A source query returns too many statement rows. What is the intended behavior?
options: Reject and require a narrower period
questions.explanation: A partial financial statement must not be silently presented as complete.

lessons.title: Trace authorization, idempotent requests and durable rendering jobs
lessons.overview: Document generation is an asynchronous state machine: accepting a request is separate from rendering a ready artifact. DocumentController verifies a customer or chef principal, normalizes the typed request and checks an Idempotency-Key. It obtains an authorized snapshot through DocumentSourceClient and stores the durable request. DocumentWorker later claims work and renders that saved snapshot. Browser input does not supply authoritative prices, an arbitrary owner, executable HTML or a storage key. The internal Academy administrator permission does not automatically authorize the customer/chef document API.

steps.label: Read the request boundary
steps.detail: The controller base is /api/v1/documents. POST requires a bearer credential, an Idempotency-Key and a typed Request. The verified principal determines the owner, while the requested document type determines whether CUSTOMER or CHEF role is required. Read Request.normalize for the exact source-ID or statement-period fields and reject unsupported shapes rather than accepting generic JSON.

steps.label: Trace replay behavior
steps.detail: For an existing owner/key pair, the repository compares the normalized request fingerprint and returns the existing result if it matches. A changed request under the same key must conflict. A lost response is not permission to create a new key immediately; first reconcile the existing request. New accepted generation responds 202, while an equivalent existing request can return 200.

steps.label: Capture authoritative source once
steps.detail: DocumentSourceClient uses the configured owned-service origins and validates the returned snapshot. Inspect source version, type, owner, currency, timestamp and bounded content. A future adapter needs those checks and ownership tests; it must not trust caller-selected totals or arbitrary URLs. Keep private snapshots out of public logs and teaching fixtures.

steps.label: Separate durable and working state
steps.detail: The stored snapshot and template version define what will be rendered. Worker claims have explicit ownership and completion behavior. The dedicated document worker is controlled by its own master and worker flags; teaching or releasing Academy does not enable these flags or unrelated Notification schedulers.

steps.label: Validate integrity before rendering
steps.detail: DocumentWorker checks the snapshot hash and template version before turning it into a PDF. A malformed or mismatched saved snapshot must fail rather than render a plausible replacement. Review retryable versus terminal failures and retain their reason so operations can investigate without repeatedly generating different documents.

steps.label: Model all client states
steps.detail: The existing document center uses generation status and bounded polling. Display accepted/pending, rendering where represented, ready and failed states accurately. A 202 response is not a downloadable PDF. Existing saved-document history uses its own opaque cursor and is not equivalent to the order screen's currently loaded first page.

lessons.example: A user presses Generate, the server accepts the request and the browser loses connectivity. Repeating the same normalized request with the same receipt must locate the same document, not create a second snapshot from possibly changed data.
lessons.lab: Trace DocumentController.create to normalization, existing receipt lookup, source authorization and repository creation. Using mocks or a disposable database, test equivalent replay, changed request under one receipt, wrong role, another owner, unavailable source, invalid snapshot version and worker failure. Record HTTP result and durable job count separately. Use scripts/documents/test-local.sh only after inspecting its disposable database setup; it must never point to a business database. Document which tests are mocked and which exercise actual SQL.
lessons.pitfall: Do not turn an accepted job into a fictional READY response to hide an unavailable renderer or storage dependency.

questions.prompt: What does HTTP 202 from a new generation request establish?
options: The document was accepted for processing
questions.explanation: Acceptance and completed rendering are separate states.

questions.prompt: Which value must not be accepted as authoritative document ownership?
questions.explanation: The browser cannot select another owner's document scope.

questions.prompt: Why store the template version with the snapshot?
options: To connect the issued artifact to its rendering contract
questions.explanation: Versioned rendering and immutable source data make the artifact reproducible and auditable.

lessons.title: Render bounded PDFs and deliver private, integrity-checked downloads
lessons.overview: Craves renders PDFs with Java PDFBox using a local canonical brand asset and typed snapshot data. It does not execute arbitrary browser HTML, download remote images or call an external AI renderer. Rendering has explicit time, page, row and byte bounds. The saved artifact is placed in private storage and downloads pass through an owner-authorized API. A private Blob container alone is not sufficient protection if a proxy leaks its content, caches a response across users or trusts an unchecked object key. Test the entire path from owned request to exact returned bytes.

steps.label: Inspect the renderer
steps.detail: Read DocumentPdfRenderer and DocumentBrand. Identify heading, table, row-wrapping, repeated-header and footer behavior. The implementation uses A4 pages, a bounded rendering deadline and page count, and a maximum four-MiB PDF. Test long descriptions and multi-page statements instead of accepting a one-line sample as pagination evidence.

steps.label: Qualify language coverage
steps.detail: Default PDF fonts do not establish support for every script. The optional CRAVES_DOCUMENTS_FONT_PATH points to an approved local font and still requires representative language tests. Verify rendering, search/copy behavior and glyph coverage for the languages actually supported. Do not distribute container font files or claim multilingual production acceptance from configuration alone.

steps.label: Preserve storage identity
steps.detail: The storage adapter receives service-controlled document keys and uses the existing managed identity/storage configuration. Do not accept arbitrary account endpoints, blob names, SAS URLs or recipients from a browser request. Keep the configured container private and verify the actual target and networking during a separately authorized document release.

steps.label: Reauthorize every download
steps.detail: DocumentController.download looks up the document for the current owner, requires READY and stored length, then asks storage to validate the expected hash and size. Possession of a document UUID is not download permission. Test a different customer's request against the same identifier and assert that no bytes are returned.

steps.label: Preserve binary response semantics
steps.detail: The controller returns application/pdf, a fixed generated attachment filename, private no-store, nosniff and a sandbox content-security policy. APIM and the web proxy must preserve the binary body and must not apply JSON rewriting. Test byte count and digest through the routed path, not merely a successful HTTP status.

steps.label: Separate artifact reuse from regeneration
steps.detail: A repeated download serves the saved artifact rather than rereading mutable menu prices or regenerating a new statement. A correction needs explicit document/version semantics, not silently replacing a previously issued file. Preserve source snapshots, hashes and audit events when investigating a download discrepancy.

lessons.example: A PDF that opens locally but is truncated through APIM fails release acceptance. Compare the generated artifact's byte count and hash with the authenticated download, then inspect the binary proxy path without logging the financial body.
lessons.lab: Run DocumentPdfRendererTest in the isolated verification workflow and inspect the generated synthetic examples. Exercise long text, page breaks, repeated headers, byte limits and any approved language/font configuration. In mocked storage tests, return a mismatched length and hash and confirm download denial. For a future controlled runtime acceptance, record storage identity, document ID, ready state, response headers, byte count and hash without exposing the snapshot or credentials. Do not generate a real invoice or email as part of the Academy publishing operation.
lessons.pitfall: A valid PDF file is not proof of correct ownership, private routing or complete financial data. Layout and access controls need separate evidence.

questions.prompt: What must happen before a document UUID can be downloaded?
options: It must appear in a screenshot
The browser must know the blob name
The API must verify current ownership and READY state
questions.explanation: An identifier is not authorization, and an accepted job is not yet a ready artifact.

questions.prompt: Why compare the routed download's hash and byte count?
options: To prove the proxy returned the exact complete stored artifact
questions.explanation: Integrity verification detects corruption or truncation across storage and proxy boundaries.

questions.prompt: Does setting a font path prove support for every language?
options: No; representative rendering and glyph tests are still required
questions.explanation: Font configuration is a prerequisite, not language acceptance evidence.

lessons.title: Handle uncertain email outcomes and extend the module safely
lessons.overview: Document email is an explicitly requested copy, not automatic receipt delivery for every payment or an unapproved monthly bulk campaign. It has a separate enablement gate and durable receipt. Before sending, the worker verifies the ready PDF and resolves the eligible account recipient through the established gateway. Once a send begins, a transport exception can mean the provider accepted the email but its acknowledgment was lost. The implementation records that ambiguous outcome as UNKNOWN rather than blindly resending. Extending the module requires source, model, rendering, client and release work together; adding an enum alone is not a complete feature.

steps.label: Trace explicit enqueue
steps.detail: POST /documents/{id}/email derives the owner from the current principal and requires its own Idempotency-Key. The request does not accept arbitrary email addresses. Follow DocumentEmailRepository to readiness, owner and quota checks, then distinguish generation status from email status in the UI.

steps.label: Locate the irreversible boundary
steps.detail: Read DocumentWorker's email branch and DocumentEmailGateway. Missing source or attachment before the send boundary can be a definite preflight failure. An exception after send begins is uncertain. Do not treat both as safely retryable merely because Java threw an exception.

steps.label: Reconcile UNKNOWN
steps.detail: Keep the original document, email receipt and provider correlation evidence. Investigate the actual provider outcome and recipient evidence before any separately approved repeat. A provider ACCEPTED result still differs from inbox delivery. Avoid logging the recipient, attachment content or credential while diagnosing the outcome.

steps.label: Add a document type deliberately
steps.detail: Start with approved financial meaning and source ownership. Add the typed source adapter, request/type contract, template version behavior, strict browser schema and focused tests. Cover wrong owner, ineligible state, large rows, snapshot integrity and download/email behavior. Do not accept arbitrary HTML, SQL, browser amounts or external URLs as a shortcut.

steps.label: Release only affected document capabilities
steps.detail: Follow the existing module runbook for a real document release: source endpoints, Notification code/schema, private storage permissions, binary gateway route and flags have separate gates. These are teaching steps, not changes being executed while publishing Academy. Preserve working general notifications, payment and delivery paths and keep secrets in their existing stores.

steps.label: Produce a complete handover
steps.detail: Record exact changed files, source SHA, tests, snapshot/template versions, storage and gateway evidence, one authorized download, cross-owner denial and an explicitly approved email/inbox check. Include feature-first rollback that keeps issued artifacts and audit history. Never clear UNKNOWN records or drop document tables to make an incident dashboard appear healthy.

lessons.example: The email provider receives an attachment but the connection times out before the response reaches Craves. An automatic retry can send two copies. UNKNOWN preserves that uncertainty until the provider outcome is reconciled.
lessons.lab: Use a mocked gateway to demonstrate preflight failure before send, successful provider acceptance and a timeout after send starts. Assert that the last case becomes UNKNOWN and is not automatically resent. Design a local-only future statement type with an approved-style meaning worksheet and a full file/test plan; do not invent tax or allocation rules. A peer must distinguish generation accepted, PDF ready, email accepted and actual inbox delivery from your evidence. Mark every live storage, provider and inbox action not executed in this training exercise.
lessons.pitfall: Blind retries can duplicate real messages. Uncertain outcomes must remain visible until reconciled rather than being converted into false success or automatic resend.

questions.prompt: A timeout occurs after the provider send begins. What is the safe recorded outcome?
questions.explanation: The provider may have accepted the message, so blind retry is unsafe.

questions.prompt: Does provider acceptance prove the recipient received the attachment in their inbox?
questions.explanation: Submission acceptance and end-recipient delivery are different events.

questions.prompt: What is required before adding a statutory or allocation-based document?
options: Approved financial meaning plus the complete owned-source and test contract
questions.explanation: Engineering cannot create statutory or financial policy merely by rendering a new document type.
